final.memo:
We have initiated a position in the newly issued sovereign bond strips of Greece, currently trading at distressed levels of 10¢ per euro [D04]. The market is currently paralyzed by fear of Eurozone contagion and the potential for a political vacuum following the upcoming June 17 election, leading to a massive mispricing of these instruments [D05].

Our analysis suggests a recovery value of 30¢ to 40¢ per euro, based on the reality that the sovereign's reliance on official-sector funding makes adherence to bailout conditions a strategic necessity for the EU and ECB [D04, D07]. By pricing these bonds at 10¢, the market is effectively ignoring the strength of the English law protections governing this post-reorg paper [D04, D05].

The path to realizing this value is clear: the sovereign must form a government capable of adhering to the conditions required for continued official-sector support [D07]. Unlike traditional corporate activism, we are not looking to reshape the boardroom, but rather to capitalize on the fact that the official sector will prioritize bailout compliance over a disorderly default [D07].

We size this at 3% of NAV to reflect our conviction in the recovery thesis while managing the risks of liquidity evaporation and political volatility [D05]. We have mitigated tail risk by layering in index puts on Euro-area financials, and we remain ready to exit if the new government deviates from the bailout agreement or if official-sector funding is halted [D05, D07].
